memory_candidates.content: When a byte/size gate needs to check a docs/ tree file, do NOT add an entry to index-entries.json / context/index.json -- that index is scoped exclusively to files under context/ (index.schema.json's own field description: 'Relative path from .claude/context/ to the file'). A sibling docs/ tree (e.g. core/docs/reference/) is never indexed there; confirmed by grep across existing docs/reference/standards/*.md files, none of which have an index-entries.json entry. Use the docs/ tree's own index file (e.g. docs-README.md) instead.

A repeatable byte-accounting harness script (print a table + total, --baseline to snapshot JSON, --compare to diff against a snapshot) is a cheap, high-leverage pattern for any 'reduce eager context surface' task: it makes every phase's claimed saving independently re-verifiable rather than trusting a hand-run wc -c that goes stale as soon as another phase touches the same files.

When a merge-source edit changes a context/ file's line count (e.g. editing a guide's Scope note), check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R (check_line_count_accuracy) will flag a stale line_count in that extension's index-entries.json. Always re-run `wc -l` and update the entry's line_count as part of the same edit, not as an afterthought discovered by a later lint run.
